In the game, her lightsabers are connected together by a fibercord at the hilt. She also threw [[starblade]]s. In the Wii, PS2, and PSP versions of [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed'' video game]], if you enter ACOLYTE as a cheat code, you can play as Asajj Ventress.''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]'' The non-canon book ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Dark Side]]'',''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Dark Side]]'' released in [[September]] [[2014]]{{DK|url=us/book/9781465418975-lego-star-wars-the-dark-side|text=LEGO Star Wars: The Dark Side}} provides her birth date as [[47 BBY/Legends|47 BBY]]. ===Original fate=== Ventress was originally supposed to be killed off in [[James Luceno]]'s novel ''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''. In [[Obsession 5|''Obsession'' 5]] ([[2005]]) it was stated that during Obi-Wan Kenobi's mission to return Ventress to the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light]] on [[Boz Pity/Legends|Boz Pity]], she received a life-threatening wound from Skywalker, faked her death and disappeared into the unknown; wishing to be free of the Jedi, the war, and Dooku. This was later overridden by the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series. [[Leland Chee]], the Keeper of the [[Holocron continuity database]], provided confirmation that any parts of the comic relating to her ultimate fate should be treated as non-[[canon]].{{Facebook|noprofile=1|url=permalink.php?story_fbid=470551479632450&id=201820953172172&comment_id=20217958&offset=0&total_comments=1|author=[[Leland Chee]]|nobackup=1}} ==="Nightsisters" inconsistency=== ''The Clone Wars'' episode "[[Nightsisters (episode)|Nightsisters]]" involves a different version of Ventress's background. As an infant, she is said to have been taken from a family of [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsisters]], rather than her original [[Rattataki/Legends|Rattataki]] species, by a slaver in order to save the rest of her tribe from suffering the same fate. A few years later her master is killed by a group of [[Weequay/Legends|Weequay]] pirates who are then fighting a Jedi, Ky Narec. Asajj performs her Force powers on one of the pirates which encourages the Jedi to make her his new apprentice. Narec is later killed fighting alongside Ventress and his death drives her to the dark side. It should also be noted that, prior to and during Narec's death she actually has hair, despite earlier statements that her [[Rattataki/Legends|species]] was naturally hairless. also depicts Ventress wielding two lightsabers both with green blades before joining forces with Dooku, but [[Republic 60|''Republic'' 60]] shows her using a blue-bladed lightsaber during and following her [[Jedi training/Legends|Jedi training]], and ''[[Star Wars: Clone Wars]]'' [[Chapter 6 (Star Wars: Clone Wars)|chapters 6]] & [[Chapter 7 (Star Wars: Clone Wars)|7]] show her with one green- and one blue-bladed lightsaber. Ventress' warlord parents, shown in ''Hate and Fear'', are also entirely absent from the new backstory. ===''Slaves of the Republic''=== When the story arc ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Slaves of the Republic]]'' was adapted for the television series' [[The Clone Wars: Season Four|fourth season]], Ventress was written out of the story due to having been abandoned by Dooku. The following details the original story. ====Storyline==== {{Quote|Pathetic, Skywalker. Her faith in your protection was as misplaced as her love.|Ventress taunting Anakin about the [[Miraj Scintel/Legends|Zygerrian queen's]] misplaced love for him.|[[The Clone Wars 5|''The Clone Wars'' 5]]}} [[File:SkywalkerVsVentressDooku.jpg|thumb|200px|right|Ventress and her master face Skywalker on [[Zygerria/Legends|Zygerria]].]] Ventress went with Count Dooku to deal with the [[Zygerria/Legends|Zygerria's]] Queen, [[Miraj Scintel/Legends|Miraj Scintel]]. Dooku sent her to deal with Anakin Skywalker and Ahsoka Tano. Though she missed her chance at getting Ahsoka, she went after Skywalker, after Dooku [[Telekinesis/Legends|Force-Choked]] the queen. Ventress taunted Skywalker, saying that his protection of her was misplaced as her love for him. The two fought each other, with Skywalker offering her the chance to surrender. He then escaped with his Padawan on Dooku's [[Solar sailer/Legends|Solar sailer]] to the [[Kadavo system/Legends|Kadavo system]] to rescue Master Kenobi, Captain [[Rex/Legends|Rex]], and the people of [[Kiros/Legends|Kiros]] as Dooku expected. Ventress, along with General Grievous, went to Kadavo to eliminate the people of Kiros to protect her master's reputation. Ventress, onboard her ship, the ''Trident'', took a squadron of [[Hyena-class bomber/Legends|''Hyena''-class bombers]] to destroy evidence of Separatist involvement. Luckily, the clone troopers were able to destroy her bomber squadron. When Ventress requested more bombers, Grievous turned her down because of Republic reinforcements, so he retreated. After this setback, Ventress took her ship and attacked the transport ship that Kenobi and Skywalker were using to help the people of Kiros. Just as she was about to destroy the transport ship, Master [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]] arrived and chased her away. ===Non-canon storyline=== After the airing of Ventress's betrayal, and subsequent revenge, [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Magazine 5|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars Magazine'' 5]] presented an [[Infinities]] scenario. Ventress returned to the Nightsisters' coven, and the Nightsisters instead imbued her with the dark magick ritual, as opposed to Savage Opress. Ventress's speed, power and agility were augmented and she was outfitted with dueling armor capable of deflecting lightsabers and blaster bolts. Asajj also added more tattoos to her face. Seeking revenge, Ventress then methodically took out all of Count Dooku's security systems and made her way into his inner sanctum to confront him in combat. Shrugging off or deflecting his Force lightning, she used her double-bladed lightsaber to tear through his defenses and put an end to him once and for all. Darth Sidious, pleased to have a younger, more powerful apprentice, knighted Ventress as '''Darth Vindicaa'''. Ventress was silently planning to eventually overthrow him as well.[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Magazine 5|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars Magazine'' 5]] ===Portrayal=== Asajj Ventress was voiced by [[Grey Griffin|Grey DeLisle]] in the [[2003]] series ''[[Star Wars: Clone Wars]]'' and the [[2008]] video game ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]'', and by [[Nika Futterman]] in the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|2008 film]] and the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|subsequent TV series]].
